jobs.occupation: Postdoc position on statistical genetics in plant breeding with special focus on cultivar mixtures in wheat
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position
The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The position provides excellent possibilities for access to state-of-the-art tools for simulation and for the analysis of complex genomic datasets, writing publications, and collaboration with industry partners as well as with other national and international research groups.

Qualifications
• Ph.D. or equivalent in plant/animal breeding, quantitative genetics, quantitative genomics, statistics, or related fields.
• Strong interest in use of stochastic models for the analysis of phenotypic and genomic data.
• Dedicated to developed statistical models in modern plant breeding
• Good understanding of methods used in genomic prediction.
• General understanding of commercial breeding programs.
• Inspiration and experience from working in a commercial breeding program will be valuable.
• Good ability to conduct large-scale computations.
• Documented skills in writing and publishing papers of the highest international standard.
• Good skills in oral and written communication in English.
• Ability to work in a large and diverse group of researchers and collaborate with national and international partners from research and industry.
Who we are:
Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG)
The institute like center, QGG, is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics () at Aarhus University. We perform basic and applied research within livestock and plant breeding as well as human applications in precision medicine. The research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development, basic analysis, and application of the developed methods on practical problems across species in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research Center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strive for an excellent working environment. We therefore value self-leadership, open communication, respect for diversity and success in mentoring, supervision and teaching. The main work location will be the main campus close to Aarhus city center.

Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Research Center Flakkebjerg, Forsøgsvej 1, 4200 Slagelse, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact Information
If you have any questions about the positions, please contact Associate Professor Bjarne Nielsen, +45 4140 9040, e-mail: Bjarne@qgg.au.dk.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.description:
The Exoplanet Group at DTU Space, Technical University of Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship exoplanet science. Our group focuses on the discovery and characterization of small planets, from rocky worlds to super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. We combine observations, data analysis, modeling, and instrument development to understand the properties and diversity of these planets and the processes that shape their evolution.

Our research has two particularly active areas. In atmospheric characterization, we study the atmospheres of small exoplanets using observations from both space- and ground-based observatories, aiming to understand their composition, evolution, and retention. Much of our current research draws on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), for which our group has led several successful observing programs (GO 2420, GO 3730, and GO 7675), alongside our involvement in numerous international collaborations, including involvement in ESA's Ariel Mission (Buchhave co-PI).

In extreme-precision radial velocity (EPRV) research, we work toward detecting and measuring low-mass planets, including through the Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES; PI: Buchhave; www.2es.dk). 2ES is a next-generation spectrograph under development for the MPG/ESO 2.2-m Telescope at La Silla, Chile, designed to search for temperate Earth-mass planets around bright southern solar-type stars. The project spans instrumentation, data analysis, stellar activity, and the preparation for commissioning and early science.

Our aim is to recruit a researcher whose scientific interests and expertise complement the group's work. The successful candidate will be free to pursue the questions in exoplanet science that they find most compelling, whether these connect directly to our current projects or bring related perspectives and methods to the group.

We consider an open and cooperative research atmosphere to be extremely important. Group members take an interest in one another's science, exchange ideas, and explore opportunities to work together. We hope to welcome a colleague who enjoys participating in such an environment while developing their own independent research.

You will join Prof. Lars A. Buchhave and Assistant Prof. Alexander Rathcke, and the growing Exoplanet Group at DTU Space (www.exoplanets.dk), located in the greater Copenhagen area. The group has access to data from world-class observatories, including JWST, precision RV spectrographs, and ESO facilities, and collaborates widely with researchers abroad.

Responsibilities and qualifications
We expect the successful candidate to develop and carry out original, independent research that complements the group's scientific interests. The specific direction will be shaped by the candidate's own interests and expertise. Possible research topics include:

 * Characterizing exoplanet atmospheres through transmission or emission spectroscopy, atmospheric retrievals and modeling, JWST data analysis, or studies of stellar contamination.

 * Detecting and characterizing low-mass planets through precision radial velocities, including RV data analysis, stellar activity mitigation, spectroscopic pipeline development, or 2ES instrumentation.

 * Pursuing other closely related observational, theoretical, or computational questions that complement the group's research on exoplanets.

We are seeking a talented and highly motivated student to work at the cutting edge of the rapidly moving research field of exoplanets. Applicants with previous experience in the mentioned areas of research are especially encouraged to apply, and we particularly value scientific initiative and strong analytical skills. Flexibility and self-motivation are desired skills, and the Exoplanet Group encourages a vibrant collaborative work environment, where collaboration with other group members is highly encouraged. In your application, we encourage you to describe how you can complement the group's scientific activities.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is flexible but would ideally commence in Q3-Q4 of 2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information and inquiries about the position can be made to Prof. Lars A. Buchhave (buchhave@space.dtu.dk) or Dr. Alexander Rathcke (rathcke@space.dtu.dk).

You can read more about the Exoplanet Group at www.exoplanets.dk and the DTU Space institute at www.space.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 January 2027 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide 2-3 reference letters to be emailed at a later date.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Space
The DTU Space Institute has about 250 employees and is located in the greater Copenhagen area at the Lyngby Campus of the Technical University of Denmark. We link natural science closely with the development of new technology. DTU Space is involved in the full life cycle of space activities, including concept and design, construction and prototyping, calibration and validation, implementation and operations, data analysis, processing, dissemination, and applications, leading to new instruments and applications. With the specialised and refined technology available, we are getting more and more answers and further insight about the Earth and the universe surrounding us. We contribute to about 200 scientific publications a year.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

This will give you hands-on experience with wind turbine control, aeroelastic simulation, MATLAB-based engineering tools and controller validation, while contributing directly to the controller software used across our turbine platforms.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• 
You will maintain and update wind turbine models using MATLAB scripts, ensuring they align with engineering specifications.

• 
Simulate turbine behavior using BHawC.

• 
Analyze simulations to identify unexpected turbine behaviour and investigate the underlying causes.

• 
Ensure the quality of the controller updates by validating that the turbine behaves as expected across different operating conditions.

• 
Update and optimize MATLAB and Python scripts for generating turbine simulation reports.

• 
Generate detailed technical reports on turbine behavior using specialized tools and LaTeX, aiding in the tuning of turbine controllers.

• 
Contribute to our engineering toolbox by improving our existing tools or developing new ones.

• 
Maintain a list of the updated turbines in Jira.

What You Bring

• 
Currently enrolled in a Master’s degree programme in Wind Energy, Mechanical, Control, Aeronautical Engineering or a similar discipline, preferably with at least 1.5 years remaining.

• 
Experience or academic coursework in MATLAB and Python, particularly in programming, data processing, analysis, visualisation and engineering simulations.

Solid understanding of wind energy engineering principles, control systems and mechanical/aeronautical engineering concepts.

• 
Proficiency in LaTeX for document preparation, technical report writing and simulation data interpretation.

Experience with Git for version control of engineering tools and scripts.

Strong critical thinking skills to analyse plots and detect outliers, ensuring the quality of each software version.

• 
Knowledge of BHawC or HawC2 would be an advantage but is not a requirement.

• 
Familiarity with Jira to keep track of the progress of your work.

• 
You are fluent in English, both written and spoken, as it is the primary language of our business.

About the Team

The Optimization & Validation team is part of the Turbine Control Department within R&D, consisting of six full-time employees and two student assistants based in a new office in Ballerup, Denmark. We are proud to be an international team with colleagues from four continents: North America, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Our team plays a key role in offshore wind turbine development projects, scoping and tuning controllers using BHawC simulations, supporting certification activities, coordinating controller changes with the Software Department, and discussing simulation results with Turbine Loads and component design teams. As projects progress towards prototype testing, we perform extensive validation activities, ensuring turbine and controller performance matches simulation predictions. Much of this work is based on data collected from our offshore turbines installed in Østerild. We encourage open technical discussions and value diverse engineering perspectives, welcoming constructive disagreement to identify problems and reach better technical decisions.

Our Commitment to Diversity

jobs.occupation: Process Engineer for advanced process solutions
jobs.description:
Do you want to develop technical process solutions for customers across the world and play a key role in transforming customer requirements into competitive and reliable industrial systems? Then this could be your next position.

On behalf of Simatek A/S, we are looking for a Process Engineer who will become a central technical resource in the company's Process & Proposal team and contribute to the continued development of customer-specific process solutions for industries worldwide.

About Simatek

Simatek A/S is an international engineering company specializing in air filtration, pneumatic conveying, dust handling, and process solutions for industries such as food, feed, grain, recycling, minerals, and industrial manufacturing. The company designs and delivers customized systems that help customers improve operational efficiency, product quality, environmental performance, and workplace safety. From its headquarters in Albertslund in Denmark, Simatek serves customers around the world and combines strong engineering expertise with a flexible and customer-oriented approach.

The position

As Process & Application Engineer, you will become part of Simatek's international Process & Proposal team with colleagues in both Denmark and India. Focusing primarily on solutions for the food, dairy, feed and grain industries, you will transform customer requirements into technically robust and commercially competitive process solutions.

Working closely with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders, you will perform process calculations, size equipment, define system configurations and contribute to the development of tailored solutions that balance technical performance, cost efficiency and customer needs.

Your responsibilities will include

• Develop process solutions based on customer requirements and application data, identifying and solving technical issues in the process design

• Perform process calculations and system sizing for complete process installations

• Prepare and review process documentation

• Collaborate with suppliers regarding technical specifications and equipment selection

• Prepare technical proposals and quotations

• Contribute to the development and standardization of engineering tools, methods and solutions

• Work closely with R&D and the product management team to develop competitive solutions

• Support continuous improvement of process design standards and engineering practices

• Participate in occasional international travel for customer and technical meetings (approx. 20 days per year)

Your profile

We imagine you have a strong engineering background and experience developing process systems or technical solutions within industrial environments.

You likely bring:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree within Process Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Energy Engineering or a related discipline

• Experience within process engineering, system design or industrial solution development, with the ability to independently drive technical tasks

• Skilled in process calculations, equipment sizing and can read PFD and P&ID drawings

• Experience in preparing technical proposals, quotations or engineering project documentation is an advantage

• Experience from the food and dairy industry will be considered an advantage

• Professional proficiency in English. An additional language will be considered an advantage

As a person, you are analytical, solution-oriented and motivated by solving complex technical challenges. You work in a structured manner, take ownership of your tasks and enjoy collaborating across technical and commercial disciplines.

Why join Simatek?

You will join an entrepreneurial organization where the distance from idea to implementation is short, allowing you to make a tangible impact.

The role offers:

• Flexible working conditions including the possibility of working from home, up to two days per week by agreement

• Attractive compensation package including pension scheme, health insurance and performance bonus

• An active social environment and employee association arranging events throughout the year

Interested?

Send your application and CV via the application button. We look forward to hearing from you.

For more information, you are very welcome to contact Senior Business Consultant Erik Bernskov at erik.bernskov@actief-hartmanns.dk or by phone at +45 41 21 13 29. All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

Actief Hartmanns manages the entire recruitment process on behalf of Simatek A/S, and all contact regarding the position should therefore be directed to us. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of age, gender, disability, ethnic background, religion or nationality.

Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been identified.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**Ready to shape how Boozt grows and develops one of its most important departments across markets?

We are looking for a Marketing Manager for a maternity cover of approximately 13 months to lead the marketing agenda for our Kids department.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of customer insight, commercial priorities, Buying strategy and marketing. You will help define what Kids should stand for at Boozt, identify the categories, themes and moments we should prioritise, and translate these into a strong marketing plan across our markets.

You will work closely with Buying & Merchandising, our market and campaign teams and specialist functions across CRM, E-commerce, Media, Brand & Creative and Social to ensure that the right Kids priorities are brought to market in the right way.

This is a role for a commercially strong marketer who combines strategic thinking with a practical understanding of what it takes to create relevant, high-performing marketing in a fast-moving e-commerce environment.

**What You Will Do

**You will be responsible for developing and continuously strengthening the Kids marketing agenda.

**Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Own the Kids marketing plan and positioning, defining the key categories, themes and customer opportunities to prioritise throughout the year, based on commercial performance, customer insight, seasonality and Buying strategy.

• Work closely with Buying & Merchandising to ensure that assortment priorities, strategic category opportunities, launches and relevant brand initiatives are translated into strong customer-facing marketing opportunities.

• Drive the Kids agenda across markets and campaigns, adapting priorities with the market/GTM team to reflect local customer needs, commercial potential and seasonality, while ensuring Kids is represented in larger Boozt campaigns with the right categories and propositions.

• Set the direction for customer-facing marketing partnering with Campaign Leads, E-commerce, CRM, Media, Brand & Creative and Social to translate Kids priorities into relevant campaigns, onsite experiences, customer journeys and content. You own the commercial direction and priorities, while specialist teams drive execution.

• Own performance and continuous improvement, using data and customer insights to measure impact, identify growth opportunities, challenge existing plans and strengthen the Kids marketing agenda.

**How The Role Works

**You will be the **marketing owner for the Kids department.

****This Means You Are Accountable For Defining

**

• what Marketing should prioritise within Kids

• why those priorities matter

• when they are relevant

• which markets they matter in

• what commercial or customer outcome they should deliver

**YOUR PROFILE

**We are looking for someone who combines strong commercial judgement with a genuine understanding of customers, categories and marketing. You know how to turn insights into clear priorities and bring people together around opportunities that drive business results.

**We Imagine That You Bring

**

• At least 5 years of experience in e-commerce, retail or consumer marketing, preferably within fashion, kidswear or a related category.

• Strong commercial understanding, connecting customer behaviour, category performance, seasonality and marketing opportunities.

• Experience developing marketing strategies and plans, translating business and customer insights into clear priorities and actionable initiatives.

• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with performance data. Experience with Qlik Sense, Google Analytics or similar tools is an advantage.

• Strong stakeholder-management skills and the ability to challenge constructively, make clear recommendations and prioritise across Buying, commercial, creative and digital teams.

• Strong marketing judgement, a high quality bar and a structured, proactive approach, combined with the flexibility to navigate a fast-moving environment.

• Fluency in English, our company language.

**WHY JOIN NOW?

**Boozt is evolving how Marketing works across markets, departments and specialist teams.

This role therefore offers the opportunity not only to lead the Kids marketing agenda during the maternity-cover period, but also to contribute to how we build a stronger, more commercially focused and more market-relevant marketing organisation going forward.

**Apply today – we’re excited to learn more about you!

**_Only applications submitted in English will be considered.

_Important: Applicants must have the legal right to work in Denmark at the time of employment. Please note that this position does not include visa sponsorship or relocation support.

We review applications on an ongoing basis. You can read more about the process under **Recruitment.

****BOOZT PERKS

**

• Great personal and internal career development opportunities

• A culture built on our values of trust, freedom, and responsibility

• Driven and passionate international colleagues

• A generous employee discount

• Healthy and delicious breakfast and lunch, top-quality coffee, and fresh fruit available all day

• In-house gym, onsite masseuse, and medical doctor

• An amazing HQ in central Copenhagen – the iconic, energy-efficient Krystallen building, recognized for its architectural design and sustainability. Enjoy breathtaking city views and much more!

**Your impact begins here

**As AI Search Specialist, you will make Novo accurately represented across AI-powered search and generative platforms. You will turn complex performance data into automated insights, scalable workflows and clear recommendations that help markets act faster. Working across regions, you will connect measurement standards with local needs, helping people find trusted health information when they need it supporting lasting health.

**What You'll Bring

**

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Digital Media, Computer Science, Data Analytics or a related field or equivalent

• 5–8 years in SEO, GEO, AEO, AI search analytics or digital performance optimisation.

• Hands-on experience with AI visibility dashboards, prompt datasets, citation data and LLM performance metrics.

• Experience building or using AI agents, automation workflows and generative AI tools professionally.

• Coding ability in Python, SQL, JavaScript or similar.

• Working knowledge of APIs, data pipelines, structured data, schema markup, CMS integrations and analytics platforms.

• Ability to translate technical insights into concise, actionable recommendations for non-technical audiences.

• Experience working across functions, markets and senior stakeholders in a global business or agency setting.

**What You'll Do

**You will own the insights platforms and automation layer of SEO and GEO across markets, moving teams from raw data to practical action.

• Build and maintain AI search dashboards tracking visibility, share of voice, citation rate, ranking, sentiment and source influence across markets .

• Analyse GEO performance across prompt clusters, LLM outputs and third-party citations. Identify gaps and turn findings into prioritised recommendations with clear owners.

• Improve discoverability and AI readability through crawlability, indexation, metadata, schema, internal linking, semantic structure and page experience.

• Develop scalable AI agents and automation workflows for insight generation, content briefs, reporting and market activation with appropriate controls.

• Connect data sources through programming, APIs and automation to cut manual analysis and speed up reporting.

• Support AI-ready content optimisation including FAQs, structured summaries, metadata and schema inputs while ensuring accuracy, compliance and alignment with relevant requirements.

**Who You'll Work With

**You will join the Digital Media Activation team in International Operations, working where data, technology and marketing meet to scale AI search optimisation across markets.

Your partners include global, regional and local digital marketing, web and content, data and analytics, brand and communications. Externally, you will work with AI visibility and SEO platform provider, such as Profound, SEMrush and SurferSEO and specialist agencies.

**What You Can Expect Here

**Real ownership in a fast-moving, cross-market environment. You will design measurement approaches, build automation and set standards that teams across regions rely on. You will sharpen your skills at the forefront of AI search, work across disciplines and markets, and contribute to helping people find accurate health information when they search for it.

**What We Offer

**At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn AI search data into scalable insights and measurable progress, **apply by November 23rd, 2026.

**We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Do you love turning menus and interfaces into something players actually enjoy clicking through, and want to own that from first sketch to final implementation? We’d love to talk to you.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're working on our most ambitious project to date: a new systemic open-world game built around a beloved IP, with our own spin on it. A bold new direction for us! And we're just getting started.

Now, we’re looking for a UI/UX Designer to join a team of around 15-20 people and own the UI/UX for the entire game. You’ll be the first dedicated UI/UX designer on the team (and at Triband generally!), so you’ll shape the game’s interface aesthetic and logic as well as player experience from the ground up.

**Here’s What You’ll Do Day To Day

**

• Own the full UI/UX pipeline for the game: from flow, wireframes, and mockups through to final in-engine implementation (we use Unity)

• Design and build UI elements like menus, icons, HUDs, and input controls that are clear, playful, and true to the game’s tone

• Bake in accessibility design and settings from the start, not as an afterthought

• Create dynamic transitions and animations that make the UI feel alive

• Implement your own designs solidly in Unity (you won’t be just handing off mockups!)

• Collaborate closely with game designers and programmers to keep the UI consistent, technically sound, and fun to use

• Maintain a consistent visual language and set of UI standards as the game grows

**You’re probably a good match if

**

• You have solid experience owning UI/UX work end to end, from flow through to final implementation

• You have strong Unity implementation skills and are comfortable taking your own UI work all the way into engine

• You’re skilled in Illustrator

• You have experience mocking up interactive flows in a tool like Figma, Miro, or similar (any tool is fine)

• You genuinely enjoy working within an existing visual style rather than starting from a blank page every time

• You’ve shipped a mobile game before, including responsive/adaptive interfaces

• You have a strong eye for color, shapes, contrast, and readability

**Nice to have

**

• A passion for accessibility and usability, especially for family-friendly/casual audiences

• You see real value in user testing and what it can teach you

• An interest in motion design and UI animation

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**This project is something new, but our ways of working are the same. We’ve always believed that games are made by teams, not solo rockstars, and good ideas can come from anyone. What we also believe in:

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward.

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You’re up for experimentation, and at the same time you don’t get too precious when the experience tells you you’re wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• This role is based in the Greater Copenhagen area, and we’re not considering people located outside of commuting distance for this one.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10–15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• A shot at shaping the interface of a live game played by millions

• A tight, collaborative team where your ideas actually make it into the game

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Private health insurance paid by us

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Noda

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide.

From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make people laugh. We explore comedy through gameplay, which means we like to break player expectations, create surprising interactions, use great music and slick art, and build quirky worlds full of personality.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games. And we believe diversity makes teams better. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and who are excited to challenge us and our way of doing things.
